title: Does Grok Generate AI Videos? 2026 Guide | Flick
summary: Yes, Grok Imagine generates short AI video clips. What it does today, how to prompt it, and how to build a full film around it on Flick.
body_text: Yes. Grok generates video through Grok Imagine: it animates still images into clips of up to 15 seconds, and it can edit or extend existing footage. The best Grok video workflow starts with a strong still image, then uses prompts to control motion, camera, style, and edits. This guide covers what Grok Imagine can do today, how to generate videos with Grok step by step, where it fits in a filmmaking workflow. It also covers Elon Musk's promised Odyssey film made entirely with Grok, an exciting project at the frontier for AI filmmaking. Quick answer: can Grok generate videos? Yes — Grok can generate videos through Grok Imagine . Question Answer Can Grok generate video? Yes, through Grok Imagine Main workflow Image-to-video Text-to-video Not on the current API preview Max clip length Up to 15 seconds Editing existing clips Yes, with prompt-based video edits Extending clips Yes, with 2–10 second extensions Reference images Yes, for visual consistency Audio Not documented in the API API pricing $0.08 per generated second Best use Fast visual exploration, stylized shots, short cinematic clips, and reference-driven filmmaking Make your film in Flick Generate with Grok and keep your characters consistent. How to use Grok on Flick, at a glance To accomplish this on Flick, start from a fresh canvas and build the shot the same way you would build any image-to-video sequence: create or upload a strong still, select it, then generate video from that image with Grok. Create a fresh project. From Flick, click New Project to open a new canvas. Choose the aspect ratio you want before generating — 16:9 for YouTube or film-style work, 9:16 for TikTok/Reels/Shorts, or 1:1 for square social posts. Set your visual style. Pick one of Flick's curated styles or upload a style reference. Flick keeps the selected style and aspect ratio pinned at the top of the canvas, so your generations stay visually consistent across the project. Create the starting image. Click the + button and choose Generate Image , or add a text node and write the image prompt there. For Grok, the starting image matters more than the text prompt because Grok Imagine is strongest as an image-to-video model. Use an image model like Nano Banana Pro, GPT Image, Midjourney, or another image model on Flick to create the exact first frame you want. Select the image and choose video. Once you have a still you like, click the image node. Flick will show options such as Generate Video , Edit Image , Change Style , and other follow-up actions. Choose Generate Video . Choose Grok as the video model. In the video model selector, pick Grok/Grok Imagine if it is available in your workspace. This keeps the whole workflow inside Flick instead of exporting the image to another tool. Write a motion prompt. Describe the camera movement, subject movement, environment movement, and constraints. Do not repeat the whole image prompt. The image already defines the frame; the video prompt should define what changes over time. Generate . Run a few versions with different camera speeds, motion intensity, or environmental details. Keep the best clip, but also keep useful frames as references for later shots. Continue the sequence on the canvas. If the shot works, use it as part of a larger scene. If you need a longer sequence, generate the next shot from a new still or an extracted frame instead of trying to force one clip to do everything. A strong first Grok prompt on Flick looks like this: Use this image as the starting frame. Slow cinematic push-in on the subject. Wind moves the cloak and background fabric, torchlight flickers, and the camera drifts slightly handheld. Preserve the character's face, outfit, and composition. No text, no extra characters, realistic motion. The key is to treat Grok as the animation pass, not the whole production pipeline. Use Flick to generate and organize the stills, references, variations, and final clips; use Grok to turn the strongest stills into motion. If you need dialogue or sound Grok's API docs do not currently document audio generation, so plan sound separately. In Flick, you can generate or attach voice/audio on the canvas, then use models that support audio-aware video when the shot requires speech. For Grok clips, treat the output as the visual layer, then add dialogue, sound design, and music in the edit. The Odyssey moment On July 22, 2026, Elon Musk posted: "Before this year ends, Grok Imagine will make a full-length movie of The Odyssey that is historically accurate and true to the art of Homer." The claim landed right after Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey opened to a massive box office run, and it instantly turned Grok Imagine from "new AI video tool" into a test case for feature-length AI filmmaking. The work Musk amplified is real, and it is worth studying. Heavy Pulp , a one-person AI filmmaker, built an Odyssey short with Grok Imagine — one artist, no crew, 4K frames. Heavy Pulp's Odyssey project, made with Grok Imagine. Credit: Heavy Pulp, via @MarioNawfal and @psyopwhite on X. That does not mean a feature film is solved. It means the frontier has moved. AI video is no longer just about whether a single clip looks cinematic. The harder problem is whether hundreds of clips can share the same character, costume, lighting, geography, and story logic. What Grok Imagine can do today Grok Imagine is best understood as an image-to-video and video-editing model. You give it a visual starting point, then use text to direct the motion and transformation. Capability Current state Model grok-imagine-video-1.5-preview Image-to-video Yes — up to 15 seconds per clip Text-to-video Not on the current API preview Video editing Yes — prompt-based edits on short clips Video extension Yes — 2 to 10 second extensions Reference-to-video Yes — uses reference images for visual consistency Audio Not documented in the API Pricing $0.08 per generated second Rate limit 60 requests/minute The important limitation: Grok Imagine does not behave like a "type a movie idea and get a finished scene" system. It works best when you provide a strong starting frame and a precise motion prompt. How to generate videos with Grok, in depth 1. Start with the right image Because Grok Imagine is image-to-video first, your input image determines most of the result. Use an image with: A clear subject. A readable silhouette. Strong lighting direction. No ambiguous hands, faces, or props. Enough background detail for camera movement. The exact style you want the video to preserve. Avoid starting from images with tiny faces, messy fingers, unreadable text, or busy backgrounds. Grok can animate them, but the weak parts of the image usually become weak parts of the video. 2. Write a motion prompt, not just a scene prompt A good Grok video prompt should describe what changes over time. Weak prompt: A warrior on a ship during a storm. Better prompt: Slow cinematic push-in on a tired Greek warrior standing at the bow of a wooden ship during a violent storm. Wind pulls their cloak backward, rain hits the lens, lightning briefly reveals waves behind them, dramatic torchlight, grounded historical epic, 35mm film look. The better prompt gives Grok: Camera motion. Subject motion. Environmental motion. Lighting changes. Style constraints. Mood and genre. 3. Keep the shot simple For reliable results, make one shot do one thing. Good Grok shot goals: A slow push-in. A profile turn. A cloak moving in wind. A ship crossing frame. A torch flickering in darkness. A monster emerging from fog. A landscape reveal. Riskier shot goals: Multi-character dialogue. Exact choreography. Complex hand interactions. Legible text. Specific logos. Continuity-heavy action. A character changing emotional beats multiple times. If you need complexity, generate several simple shots and cut them together. 4. Generate variations Do not expect the first generation to be the final shot. Treat Grok like a fast visual exploration tool. Generate variations around: Camera speed. Lens language. Lighting. Weather. Wardrobe motion. Subject direction. Amount of stylization. Realism vs. painterly texture. Save the best results, but also save the best still frames. Those frames can become references for later shots. 5. Extend only when the clip is stable Grok can extend existing footage, but extensions amplify problems. If the original 5–10 seconds already has face drift, broken hands, or confusing motion, extension usually makes those issues worse. Extend clips when: The subject identity is stable. The motion has a clear direction. The background is coherent. The shot has not already reached its natural endpoint. You need a little more handle for editing. Do not extend just because you want a longer clip. In AI video, a tighter 6-second shot often looks more professional than a stretched 15-second shot. 6. Edit with prompts Grok can also edit footage with text prompts. Use edits for targeted changes: Add fog. Make the camera slower. Increase torchlight. Make the sea rougher. Change time of day. Add sparks, rain, dust, or smoke. Push the style more cinematic or more documentary. Keep edits specific. A prompt like "make it better" gives the model too much freedom. A prompt like "keep the same composition, add heavier rain and slower camera movement" is much safer. Grok video prompt template Use this structure: [Camera movement] on [main subject] in [setting]. [Subject motion]. [Environmental motion]. [Lighting]. [Style / lens / texture]. [Constraints: preserve identity, no text, no extra characters, realistic motion]. Example: Slow handheld tracking shot behind an exhausted Greek soldier walking through a torchlit palace corridor. The soldier limps slightly and keeps one hand on the wall for balance. Smoke drifts through the hallway, torch flames flicker, distant shadows move across stone columns. Warm firelight, deep contrast, historical epic, 35mm film grain. Preserve the character's face and armor, no modern objects, no readable text, no extra characters. Prompt examples for Grok Imagine Cinematic character shot Slow cinematic push-in on a weathered sailor standing at the bow of an ancient wooden ship. Wind pulls their cloak backward, rain hits their face, and lightning briefly reveals huge waves behind them. Moody torchlight, grounded historical epic, realistic motion, 35mm film look. Preserve the subject's identity and costume, no extra people, no text. Monster reveal Locked-off wide shot of a dark cave entrance on a rocky island. A massive cyclops silhouette slowly steps into the moonlight, dust falling from the cave ceiling. Cold blue moonlight, drifting fog, realistic scale, tense mythological atmosphere. No text, no modern objects, no cartoon style. Product-style motion test Slow studio orbit around a futuristic black camera on a reflective table. Soft light sweeps across the lens glass, subtle particles float in the air, background stays minimal. Premium commercial style, crisp details, realistic reflections. Keep the object shape consistent, no logos, no text. Documentary-style shot Handheld documentary shot of a lone traveler crossing a sunburned desert road. Heat shimmer rises from the ground, dust moves across the frame, the camera shakes slightly as if filmed by a person walking. Natural light, muted colors, realistic motion, no stylized fantasy elements. Grok Odyssey-style epic shot Wide cinematic shot of ancient Greek ships approaching a rocky island at dawn. Sails move in the wind, oars cut through dark water, mist wraps around the cliffs. Epic historical realism, warm sunrise, 70mm film texture, grounded scale. No modern objects, no text, no extra fantasy elements. Grok vs. other AI video models Model/workflow Best for Watch-outs Grok Imagine Fast image-to-video, stylized cinematic exploration, short clips No preview API text-to-video, 15-second clip ceiling, continuity drift Seedance Reference-heavy filmmaking workflows and character consistency Requires careful reference pack setup Kling Strong motion, stylized action, and character-focused shots Can still drift across longer sequences Veo High-end realism and polished shots Access and workflow vary Flick canvas Managing multiple models, references, edits, grades, and timeline continuity Depends on choosing the right model per shot Grok is not automatically the best model for every shot. Its value is speed, accessibility, and visual energy. For a finished film, you will usually want Grok as one model inside a broader workflow rather than the only tool. What Grok can't do yet The current limits are straightforward: No text-to-video on the preview API. Start from an image. Short clips only. Up to 15 seconds per generation. Continuity is fragile. Characters can drift across generations. Text and logos are unreliable. Do not depend on perfect on-screen typography. Audio is not documented. Plan sound separately. Complex interactions are risky. Hands, fights, dialogue, and exact choreography still need careful iteration. None of this makes Grok weak. It means you should use it like a shot generator, not a full production pipeline by itself. Could Grok actually make a feature-length Odyssey? Do the math. At 15 seconds per generation, a 100-minute film is roughly 400 clips. Every clip needs the same Odysseus: same face, same wardrobe, same scar, same lighting logic, same world, same emotional arc. Today's Grok Imagine can create striking shots, but feature-length continuity is a different problem. Feature-length AI film is not blocked by clip quality anymore. It is blocked by production management: Reference management. Shot organization. Character continuity. Costume continuity. Location continuity. Color grading across hundreds of generations. Editing rhythm. Sound, music, and dialogue. Version control. That is why one-person filmmakers like Heavy Pulp matter. They are proving the real workflow: generate strong shots, organize references, repair continuity, and cut the project like a film. Common mistakes to avoid Expecting text-to-video from the preview API. Grok Imagine currently starts from images. Writing static prompts. Video prompts need motion, not just description. Making every shot too long. Shorter clips often look more professional. Ignoring continuity. A single good clip does not make a sequence. Overusing extensions. Extensions can magnify artifacts. Relying on generated text. Use post-production for titles, labels, and logos. Comparing raw generations only. Grade, cut, and sequence the clips before deciding whether they work. Frequently Asked Questions Does Grok generate videos? Yes. Grok Imagine animates still images into video clips of up to 15 seconds, and can edit and extend existing clips. It does not currently generate video from text alone on the preview API. How do I generate a video with Grok? Start with a strong image, write a motion-focused prompt, generate variations, pick the most stable result, then edit or extend only if the shot remains coherent. Can Grok do text-to-video? Not on the current API preview. Generations start from an image; text prompts direct the motion, camera, style, and edits. How long can Grok Imagine videos be? Up to 15 seconds per generated clip, with 2–10 second extensions on existing footage. Is Grok Imagine free? The API is paid at $0.08 per generated second of output. Can Grok make a full movie? It can generate short clips that could be used in a movie, but a feature-length film requires continuity across hundreds of shots. That is a production workflow problem, not just a model capability question. Who made the Grok Odyssey video? The short Musk amplified is by Heavy Pulp, a solo AI filmmaker working with Grok Imagine. Musk separately promised a full-length Odyssey from Grok Imagine before the end of 2026. What did Elon Musk promise? On July 22, 2026, Musk posted that Grok Imagine will make a full-length Odyssey film "historically accurate and true to the art of Homer" before year end. Mentions: Human-in-the-Loop AI Agents at FurtherAI
summary: FurtherAI's new Mentions feature lets AI agents pause and tag a person when a workflow needs human judgment, then pick the work back up once the call is made.
body_text: Today we're launching Mentions in FurtherAI. When an AI agent reaches a step that needs human judgment, it pauses the workflow and tags the right person, the same way you'd @mention a coworker in Slack. That person opens the mention, sees the exact step and its full context, makes the call, and the agent picks the work back up. No one has to sit and watch the run. Micromanaging is bad for humans. It turns out it's not great for AI either. Most insurance workflows aren't fully autonomous, and forcing a person to monitor every run just to catch the one moment their input matters wastes the time the automation was supposed to give back. Why insurance workflows still need a human in the loop An agent can handle most of an underwriting or claims workflow on its own, from classifying documents and extracting data to running checks, standardizing loss runs, and drafting a summary. But most workflows aren't end to end, and certain steps still need human judgment or a sign-off. Before Mentions, catching those moments meant reviewing everything. Someone had to stay close to a run just to be there when their input mattered, which is a poor use of an expert's time and undercuts the point of automating the rest. How Mentions works Mentions gives the agent a way to ask for help without stopping everything or handing the whole task back to you. Here's the flow: The agent runs the workflow until it hits a step flagged for human review. It pauses at that step and creates a mention for the specific person who owns that decision. That person gets the mention in a dedicated Mentions tab, with an open count so nothing slips through. They open it, see the exact step, the account, and the full context the agent has gathered so far. They make the decision and resume the workflow with one click. The agent continues through the remaining steps and marks the mention resolved. Each mention carries the details you need to act fast: the account name, the workflow it belongs to, the step that's paused, who it's assigned to, and how long it's been waiting. Open mentions and resolved ones live in separate views, so your queue always reflects what still needs a human. ‍ ‍ What this looks like in a real workflow Take a property submissions workflow, one of the more involved ones an underwriting team runs. The agent moves through 17 steps on its own, from receiving the submission and extracting account and ACORD data to running clearance and OFAC checks, aggregating loss runs, calculating a triage score, completing adverse media research, and generating the underwriting summary . Then it reaches a step that needs a sign-off, reviewing the Salesforce data, and pauses. The agent mentions the underwriter who owns the account. They click into the open item, land on that specific workflow with the full context for the decision, and approve the step to unblock the agent. It creates the opportunity in Salesforce, finishes the run, and the mention moves to resolved. Why this matters for underwriting and claims teams Mentions changes what "automation" has to mean for your team. You no longer have to choose between a workflow that runs fully on its own and one a person supervises end to end. The agent does the work, and, in the words of FurtherAI's Insurance Product Lead Danny O'Lenic, "instead of reviewing everything, you're pulled in when judgment is necessary." That keeps accountability where it belongs, with a clear record of who made which decision and when, and it keeps your underwriters and adjusters focused on high-value work instead of watching progress bars. Mentions are live in FurtherAI today. ‍ DISCLAIMER This article is for general informational purposes only and does not constitute legal, regulatory, compliance, underwriting, or other professional advice. The content reflects information available as of the date of publication, and FurtherAI undertakes no obligation to update it as laws, regulations, or AI technologies evolve. ‍

title: An Ergonomic Workspace Strategy Lowers Health Costs
summary: Learn how an ergonomic workspace strategy lowered health costs, cut MSK claimants 34%, and helped 87% of employees work more comfortably.
body_text: Issue Musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions were the second-highest driver of healthcare spend for this organization. Additionally, employee survey feedback cited workstation discomfort as negatively impacting the daily employee experience, with improvements to workstation ergonomics identified as a top opportunity to enhance health and wellbeing at work. Together, these factors indicated a need for a proactive, environment-based intervention. Solution The organization invested in a comprehensive ergonomic redesign of all workstations. In partnership with a workplace ergonomist, each workstation across the district was assessed and prioritized, resulting in a phased three-year implementation plan led by a dedicated CBIZ Wellbeing Coordinator. This initiative targeted the root causes of repetitive strain and poor posture, key drivers of musculoskeletal conditions. Outcome Since beginning the ergonomic workstation replacement, the organization has seen measurable improvements in employee wellbeing and a meaningful reduction in musculoskeletal claims and costs. Early results following full implementation suggest the investment is translating into measurable risk reduction and improved employee experience. Health and Claims Improvements 20% to 30% reduction in employees experiencing MSK-related issues during the rollout, with the lowest number of MSK claimants occurring after full ergonomic implementation 45% reduction in claim volume during the first post-implementation reporting period 34% reduction in unique claimants 7% reduction in claims per 1,000 member-months Financial Impact 23% reduction in total MSK spend during the first months following full workstation deployment MSK dropped from the second-highest cost driver to the fifth, reducing its overall financial burden on the health plan Remaining high-cost claims were largely tied to unavoidable surgical cases rather than posture- or repetitive strain-related diagnoses Employee Feedback 87% of employees reported improved workstation comfort and usability 85% of employees who previously experienced discomfort reported reduced pain or improved physical comfort 77% reported improved productivity or a greater ability to do their best work Company Information Industry Education Geographic Footprint Kansas City Area Number of Employees 650 © Copyright CBIZ, Inc. title: TrussPoint Builds Foundation for Residential Exterior Growth with ServiceTitan
summary: LOS ANGELES – July 7, 2026 – ServiceTitan (Nasdaq: TTAN), the software platform that powers the trades, today announced that TrussPoint Roofing & Exterior Renovations, a growth-oriented investment platform focused on residential home exterior services, has selected ServiceTitan to help support continued growth across its expanding portfolio of roofing brands.
body_text: Leading Residential Exteriors Platform Leverages ServiceTitan to Support Expansion Across its Growing Portfolio of Founder-Led Brands LOS ANGELES – July 7, 2026 – ServiceTitan (Nasdaq: TTAN), the software platform that powers the trades, today announced that TrussPoint Roofing & Exterior Renovations , a growth-oriented investment platform focused on residential home exterior services, has selected ServiceTitan to help support continued growth across its expanding portfolio of roofing brands. “TrussPoint has built a unique model centered on investing in people and helping founder-led businesses realize their full potential,” said Nina Katsman, General Manager of Exteriors at ServiceTitan. “By combining local expertise with a shared operational platform, TrussPoint is creating a scalable foundation for growth while preserving the cultures and customer relationships that make each brand successful. We’re proud to support their continued expansion and help enable the next phase of growth across their portfolio.” Backed by Soundcore Capital Partners, TrussPoint has quickly established itself as a leading platform in the residential roofing and exterior services sector since its founding in 2025, supporting brands including Ridge Top Exteriors , Mario’s Roofing , Eaton Roofing & Exteriors and Runyon & Sons Roofing . As TrussPoint continues to expand its footprint, ServiceTitan will serve as the operational backbone supporting alignment and visibility across the organization while helping local brands maintain the cultures and customer experiences that have fueled their success. “We believe the best businesses are built by the people who know their customers and communities best,” said Chad Colony, Chief Executive Officer of TrussPoint. “Our role is not to replace what makes these companies special, but to provide the resources, processes and support that allow them to realize their full potential. ServiceTitan provides a scalable foundation that helps our teams operate more efficiently while creating new opportunities for growth across the organization.” TrussPoint partners with family-owned businesses to help them scale while preserving the local relationships, expertise, and cultures that have made them successful. By providing resources, processes, and support, the company enables local teams to continue doing what they do best, while creating new opportunities for employees and leaders across the organization. “When we joined TrussPoint, it was important to us that we preserve the culture and reputation we’ve spent decades building,” said Stephen Goulston, Founder of Mario's Roofing. “ServiceTitan has become an important part of that foundation, providing greater visibility into our business and helping us streamline operations so we can continue delivering exceptional service to customers.” For more information about ServiceTitan, visit https://www.servicetitan.com/roofing . About ServiceTitan ServiceTitan is AI for the trades—a purpose-built agentic operating system designed to automate the workflows that run a contracting business, from enterprise commercial construction to residential field service, exteriors and beyond. The company’s end-to-end solution gives contractors the tools they need to run and grow their business, while providing a stellar customer experience. Learn how ServiceTitan is equipping tradespeople with the AI technology they need to keep the world running at: www.servicetitan.com About TrussPoint TrussPoint was created in 2025 as a platform in the residential roofing and exterior services sector. Today, TrussPoint supports a growing portfolio of leading regional brands, including Ridge Top Exteriors, Mario’s Roofing, Eaton Roofing & Exteriors, and Runyon & Sons Roofing. TrussPoint is focused on high-growth, retail-centered, vendor-managed repair and maintenance roofing and exterior services companies. title: Otter Claim Solutions Is Kyber Certified, Setting a New Standard for Adjuster Readiness
summary: Otter Claim Solutions’ adjusters have completed Kyber’s training program, reinforcing a shared commitment to faster ramp-up, stronger workflows, and high-quality, AI-supported correspondence for the carriers both teams support.
body_text: Claims organizations often need to scale quickly, especially in catastrophe-prone regions where new adjusters and external partners may step into active workflows with little notice. Carriers already invest significant time in onboarding and preparing their teams, and Kyber’s certification program is designed to complement that work by giving external partners a shared foundation before they begin supporting live workflows. For partners like Otter Claims, certification creates a portable training standard that helps teams enter Kyber-enabled environments with more confidence, stronger platform fluency, and the ability to use AI tools effectively from day one. Otter Claims Leads the Way As the first TPA to complete Kyber certification training, Otter Claim Solutions is setting an early example for what adjuster readiness can look like across the broader claims ecosystem. “Completing Kyber’s certification program reflects the level of readiness we aim to bring to every client engagement,” said Elizabeth Popkins, SVP Sales & Operations at Otter Claim Solutions. “It gives carriers confidence that our team can step into new workflows quickly and deliver consistent, high-quality, and compliant communication from day one.” The milestone reflects Otter’s commitment to investing in its people and preparing adjusters to operate effectively in modern, technology-enabled claims environments. Kyber’s New Certification Program Kyber created its certification program to help every user develop practical fluency across the platform’s correspondence workflows, review processes, and AI-supported drafting capabilities. When claims teams expand capacity, readiness matters. Adjusters need to understand established workflows , communicate clearly, and produce correspondence that aligns with carrier expectations. Certification gives TPAs and independent adjusters an additional layer of preparation before they begin working in Kyber-enabled environments. “Kyber’s training program is about helping the entire claims ecosystem move faster while maintaining quality,” said Arvind Sontha, Founder and CEO of Kyber. “That means understanding both the workflow and how to use AI within it. When adjusters have that foundation, they can support carriers more effectively from the start.” What Kyber Certification Covers Kyber’s certification program helps users build practical fluency across the full correspondence workflow, including: AI Letter creation and editing Managing review cycles & workflow management Sending communications via omnichannel delivery Using in-editor AI and AI drafting features effectively The program also includes AI fluency training, helping users understand how to use Kyber’s AI capabilities to create compliant, personalized, carrier-aligned output. Read more about Kyber’s training platform here . A Win for the Broader Claims Ecosystem This milestone reflects positively on the carriers Kyber and Otter serve. Carrier onboarding remains foundational, and certification strengthens that work by giving external teams a shared baseline before they support live workflows. That translates into faster ramp times, smoother collaboration, and greater confidence in the consistency and quality of communications produced across internal and external teams. Kyber built this program to support how claims organizations operate today. Otter’s participation shows how training can extend beyond a single organization and help raise the standard across the broader ecosystem. As more TPAs and adjusters complete the program, the goal is simple: teams that are ready to step in, align quickly, and deliver high-quality work from the start. ‍

title: Casella Unveils New RNG Facility with Waga Energy
summary: Casella Waste Systems, Inc. and Waga Energy partner to create renewable natural gas from landfill gas at the Chemung County Landfill in Elmira, NY.
body_text: 2026-05-15 14:06 Press release Casella Unveils New RNG Facility with Waga Energy Pictured from left to right: Chemung Town Supervisor George Richter, Chemung County Executive Chris Moss, Casella President & CEO Ned Coletta, Waga Energy CEO Guénaël Prince, Valley Energy CEO Ed Rogers Casella Waste Systems, Inc., a regional solid waste, recycling, and resource management services company in the Eastern United States, and Waga Energy, a global expert in the production of Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) from landfills, held a ribbon-cutting ceremony on May 14, 2026, to celebrate the opening of the RNG production facility at the Chemung County Landfill in Elmira, New York. The facility, which has been successfully turning landfill gas into RNG since January 2026, represents a key milestone in Casella’s efforts to create valuable resources from waste. “We’re excited to celebrate the opening of this facility as it represents a key piece of our strategy coming to life,” said Ned Coletta, President and CEO of Casella Waste Systems, Inc. “We made the decision several years ago to find great partners to develop these RNG projects at our facilities rather than invest the capital and embark on projects that are outside the scope of our expertise. This project is a great example of the benefits of that approach as we see the collective expertise of Chemung County, Waga Energy, and our landfill operations team coming together to create value out of the waste we manage.” The facility leverages the WAGABOX® technology developed and patented by Waga Energy to upgrade landfill gas into pipeline‑quality RNG. The RNG produced on-site is injected directly into the Valley Energy natural gas distribution network, supplying the region with a renewable alternative to fossil natural gas. The facility is designed to generate up to 610,000 MMBtu of renewable gas annually and is expected to avoid more than 47,000 tons of CO2‑equivalent emissions each year, according to U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) standards [1] . Through its first four months, the facility has performed well through its ramp-up phase, and is projected to produce 340,000 MMBtu in year one, which is equivalent to 2.4 million gallons of diesel fuel. "We are honored to celebrate this inauguration alongside Casella, a company whose commitment to sustainability and environmental stewardship is truly exemplary,” said Guénaël Prince, Chief Executive Officer of Waga Energy Inc. “The successful commissioning of the Chemung facility demonstrates the strength of our partnership and Casella's leadership in renewable energy development. This project showcases how innovative collaboration can turn waste into a valuable resource for the energy transition, benefiting both the environment and local communities." Under the terms of the agreement, Waga Energy deployed the capital required to fully fund the construction of the facility and will own and operate the facility for 20 years, while Casella and Waga Energy share the revenue generated from RNG sales. [1] Landfill Gas Energy Benefits Calculator | US EPA Topics: Landfill Sustainability About Casella Waste Systems, Inc. Casella Waste Systems, Inc., headquartered in Rutland, Vermont, is one of the largest recyclers and most experienced fully integrated resource management companies in the Eastern United States. Founded in 1975 as a single truck collection service, Casella has grown its operations to provide solid waste collection and disposal, transfer, recycling, and organics services to more than one million residential, commercial, municipal, institutional, and industrial customers and provides professional resource management services to over 10,000 customer locations in more than 40 states. title: Vertiv Introduces Vertiv DynaFlex Battery Energy Storage System, To Support Energy Grid Independence for Mission Critical Applications in North America and EMEA
summary: Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today introduced the Vertiv™ DynaFlex BESS, a battery energy storage system designed to enable energy independence and bolster sustainability efforts at mission critical facilities.
body_text: Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today introduced the Vertiv™ DynaFlex BESS , a battery energy storage system designed to enable energy independence and bolster sustainability efforts at mission critical facilities. Available today in North America and EMEA, the Vertiv DynaFlex BESS provides flexibility in the use of utility power and is a critical step in the deployment of a dynamic power architecture. The system allows organizations to fully leverage the capabilities of hybrid power systems that include solar, wind, hydrogen fuel cells, and other forms of alternative energy. The lithium-ion batteries in the Vertiv DynaFlex BESS provide utility-scale energy for long duration support, allowing seamless and repeated transitions between energy sources. When paired with the optional Vertiv™ DynaFlex EMS (Energy Management System), the Vertiv DynaFlex BESS enables advanced energy management strategies, such as demand management and sharing or selling energy back to the grid that can result in a reduction of utility energy consumption and costs and potentially generate revenue for the parties involved. According to Omdia’s Market Landscape: Battery Energy Storage Systems report, “Enabling the battery ESS to interact with the smart electric grid is an innovative way of contributing to the grid through the balance of energy supply and demand, the integration of renewable energy resources into the power equation, the reduction or deferral of grid infrastructure investment, and the creation of new revenue streams for stakeholders.” “Sustainability has become a core tenet of many organizations’ growth plans, but concerns about operational resilience and growing stress on the grid have limited efforts to adopt alternative energy sources,” said Peter Panfil, vice president, global power, Vertiv. “The Vertiv™ DynaFlex BESS opens the full energy management toolbox. It allows organizations to leverage the strengths of these new energy generation assets and relegates the traditional utility provider to a complementary role in a more dynamic, efficient, and reliable mix of energy sources.” The Vertiv DynaFlex BESS is designed specifically for mission critical environments, such as commercial industrial facilities, high-value manufacturing plants, data centers, and other facilities where power plays a critical role. The system’s power conversion system (PCS) is designed to support 2 millisecond output, virtually eliminating any delays while shifting the load between hybrid power sources. Paired with an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system, the reliable, highly efficient design of the Vertiv DynaFlex BESS reduces the risk of data center outages and diesel generator starts. The UL9540A-tested lithium-ion batteries in the Vertiv DynaFlex BESS are designed to minimize fire risks, are free-standing with a small footprint, and are designed for modularity. For more information on the Vertiv DynaFlex BESS and other innovative power solutions from Vertiv, visit Vertiv.com . About Vertiv Vertiv (NYSE: VRT) brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to enable its customers’ vital applications to run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today’s data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extends from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, USA, Vertiv does business in more than 130 countries. For more information, and for the latest news and content from Vertiv, visit Vertiv.com . title: Enterprise AI Failure Rate: 10 Ways to an AI Graveyard
summary: The enterprise AI failure rate is 95%. Explore the 10 most common reasons AI pilots die in operations—from data gaps to governance failures.
body_text: The AI graveyard describes a common pattern behind the enterprise AI failure rate: strong AI ambition, promising pilots, and poor operational outcomes. Many initiatives work in controlled environments but fail when exposed to messy data, legacy systems, human workflows, and unclear accountability. This infographic outlines the practical reasons AI fails after the demo stage and provides a structured view of what breaks between pilot, deployment, scale, and day-to-day operations so you can plan for execution, not just experimentation. Why AI Graveyard Initiatives Fail Structural Issue: Many AI deployments rely on fragmented data, disconnected systems, and infrastructure that was never designed for real-time decisioning. What succeeds in a pilot often cannot survive enterprise variability, latency, and integration complexity. Operational Issue: AI performance often drops when interaction volumes increase, escalation paths fail, or human handoffs create friction. At scale, orchestration and operational design matter as much as model quality. Governance or Measurement Issue: Ownership is often split across IT, Operations, Data, and business teams, with no clear SLA or accountability model. Without governance, trust, recovery, and ROI measurement break down quickly. Why This Requires a Different Operating Model The AI graveyard is not caused by model quality alone. It is usually the result of deploying AI into workflows, systems, and governance structures that were not rebuilt for operational use. This is why AI is not a simple tool deployment. Leadership alignment across technology, operations, data, security, and business ownership determines whether AI can scale with control, trust, and measurable ROI. The execution model—not the pilot—usually determines enterprise outcomes.

title: Native American DNA Test | 3 things to know before buying
summary: If you are considering buying a Native American DNA test kit, you should know some important things before you start!
body_text: 3 Tips for Native American Ancestry Testing | Genomelink ‍ Interested in learning about your Native American ancestry through DNA testing ? While these tests can provide fascinating insights, it’s essential to understand their capabilities and limitations—especially when identifying specific tribes or determining cultural ties. Here’s an updated guide on what to expect and the best DNA kits for exploring Native American ancestry. ‍ DNA Test vs. Tribal Identity While DNA testing can be a fascinating tool to uncover Indigenous American ancestry, it is important to understand that genetic data alone does not define tribal identity or guarantee tribal membership. Tribal identity in the United States is deeply rooted in culture, family ties, and community connection, and each federally recognized tribe operates as a sovereign nation with the right to establish its membership criteria. This often includes tracing lineage to individuals listed on historic tribal rolls or meeting specific blood quantum requirements—standards that were influenced historically by U.S. government policies but are now controlled by individual tribes. Genetic testing companies like AncestryDNA and 23andMe emphasize that their tests are designed to identify genetic patterns rather than establish cultural or legal ties to any tribe. AncestryDNA explains that their results reflect genetic inheritance without addressing the social and cultural connections integral to tribal identity, which are determined by tribal nations rather than genetics. Similarly, 23andMe notes that their results can reveal Indigenous American ancestry broadly but should not be considered proof of tribal affiliation. They specify that the presence of Indigenous American DNA in one’s genetic profile only provides evidence of distant ancestral origins and does not confer any legal or cultural status. Tribal identity is a multifaceted concept that encompasses shared traditions, cultural practices, and a sense of community belonging. While some individuals use DNA tests to reconnect with Indigenous heritage, tribes continue to uphold their criteria for membership, which are often shaped by history, laws, and cultural values. For those looking to understand their connection to a tribe, exploring family history, consulting with tribal authorities, and engaging in cultural education can be more meaningful pathways than relying on DNA results alone. Understanding the distinction between genetic heritage and cultural identity allows for a respectful approach to Indigenous ancestry, recognizing that tribal membership is grounded in community, not DNA alone. ‍ 1. What a “Native American” DNA Test Can (and Cannot) Reveal DNA tests for Native American ancestry provide a broad look at Indigenous heritage, typically without specifying affiliations with particular tribes, such as Cherokee, Navajo, or Lakota. Instead, companies categorize Indigenous ancestry under broad labels like “Native American” or “Indigenous Americas,” which cover wide regions across North, Central, and South America. This generalized approach is partly due to limited participation from Native American communities in commercial DNA databases, stemming from a history of privacy and exploitation concerns. Testing companies like FamilyTreeDNA and 23andMe and others trace Indigenous ancestry to ancient migrations from Asia, highlighting shared markers across Native American populations. 23andMe , for instance, includes the Ancestry Composition Report , which estimates the proportion of your DNA linked to Indigenous Americas ancestry over the last 500 years. Additionally, they provide insights into eight specific North American regional genetic groups, including the Northeast, Great Lakes, South Central, and Southwest regions, based on shared patterns among certain populations. Genomelink’s Native American Report goes beyond standard ethnicity estimates by focusing on your connections to Native American populations like the Pima, Yakut, and South American tribes. This report highlights which parts of your genome are linked to Indigenous groups and analyzes your genetic heritage in the Americas. ‍ 2. Best DNA Test Kits for Native American Ancestry If you’re ready to explore your Native American ancestry, choosing a DNA kit with specific tools for Indigenous analysis can help you get the most from your results. Here are some of the top options: 1. FamilyTreeDNA FamilyTreeDNA (FTDNA) offers comprehensive tools to explore Indigenous ancestry across maternal and paternal lines. Autosomal DNA Test : This test scans thousands of genetic markers across your genome to detect general Native American ancestry, though it does not identify specific tribes. Y-DNA Test (Paternal Lineage) : This test traces paternal ancestry through the Y-chromosome, passed from father to son, making it helpful for men tracing Native American ancestry on their father’s side. Female users can ask a male relative to take the test. mtDNA Test (Maternal Lineage) : This test traces maternal ancestry through mitochondrial DNA, which passes from mother to child, providing ancient insights into Indigenous connections along the maternal line. FTDNA’s various testing options make it a strong choice for exploring both sides of your ancestry. 2. AncestryDNA AncestryDNA is popular for its extensive database, which enhances its ethnicity estimates. The test compares your DNA with Indigenous populations across the Americas, providing an overview of Native American ancestry. While it doesn’t specify tribes, AncestryDNA offers family tree-building tools and a DNA matching feature that connects you with potential relatives who share Indigenous ancestry. This is ideal if you want to create a family tree and trace family connections. AncestryDNA clarifies that having Indigenous American DNA does not equate to tribal citizenship. The platform recognizes that tribal identity is based on cultural and community connections rather than solely on genetics. 3. 23andMe 23andMe includes robust tools for exploring Native American ancestry. Its Ancestry Composition Report reveals the percentage of your DNA linked to Indigenous Americas ancestry, typically reflecting connections over the last 500 years. The report also highlights eight regional genetic groups within North America—such as Alaska, Great Basin, Northeast, and Southwest —offering a deeper look into ancestral regions linked to specific Native American communities. Additionally, 23andMe provides haplogroup information that traces ancient maternal and paternal lineages, which may include Indigenous ancestry markers. These insights help map ancient migration patterns, making it a well-rounded option for those interested in Indigenous heritage and health insights. ‍ ‍ Comparative Analysis The Native American ancestry reports from 23andMe, AncestryDNA, Family Tree DNA offer varied approaches, each with unique features and limitations. Only 23andMe and Family Tree DNA include haplogroup analysis, which traces ancient maternal and paternal lineages, though this analysis still cannot determine specific tribal affiliations. All three companies provide broad regional insights, positioning themselves as tools for initial exploration rather than definitive evidence of tribal identity. For users interested in formal recognition or connection with Native American communities, supplementing DNA insights with detailed genealogical documentation and community engagement remains essential. ‍ 3. Best Upload Sites for Exploring Native American Ancestry Already taken a DNA test? Uploading your data to specialized sites can provide additional insights into Indigenous ancestry. Here are some top options: Genomelink Native American Report and Deep Ancestry Report Learn about your Native American ancestry through DNA testing with Genomelink! Genomelink tests can provide insights that are essential to understanding your roots. Genomelink’s Native American Report allows users to upload raw DNA data for specialized analysis of Native American ancestry, highlighting connections to specific Indigenous populations like the Pima, Yakut, and ancient South American tribes. This report offers more detailed insights than standard ethnicity estimates, providing context to your Native American roots. The Genomelink Deep Ancestry Report offers a thorough view of Native American and broader genetic heritage, featuring over 100 ethnic and regional labels. It provides confidence in ancestry results with detailed statistical analysis and reliability scores. Organized in three tiers, the report starts with a broad continental overview, then moves to sub-regional details, and finally pinpoints specific regions, offering precise insights from major origins to specific areas. This structured approach allows a nuanced understanding of your Native American ancestry and overall genetic background. GEDmatch GEDmatch is widely used by genealogists for its advanced analysis tools. By uploading your raw DNA data, you gain access to features like the One-to-Many match tool, which helps identify relatives with shared Native American ancestry. GEDmatch also allows users to split DNA data by maternal and paternal lines, enabling detailed exploration of your family tree. Though it may have a learning curve, GEDmatch is ideal for those interested in advanced genetic genealogy. ‍ Final Thoughts: Should You Get a Native American DNA Test? DNA testing offers an intriguing look into Native American ancestry, but it doesn’t determine tribal membership or identity. Kits from FamilyTreeDNA, AncestryDNA, 23andMe provide a broad view of Indigenous roots, while upload sites like Genomelink and GEDmatch enable deeper exploration. For those seeking meaningful cultural connections, the Bureau of Indian Affairs and Department of the Interior provide guidance on respectful ways to connect with Native American heritage. Remember, DNA testing is just one part of understanding Native American heritage. Consider it a starting point to learn more about your roots and cultural connections in a respectful and meaningful way. ‍ We hope you found this “ 3 Tips for Native American Ancestry Testing | Genomelink ” post both interesting and useful. I’d love to hear your experiences with the products and services I’ve listed above or anything else you’ve tried. Please tell us your comments and share what you’ve found by emailing us at info@genomelink.io . ‍ If you are interested and have time to do this research yourself, check out our posts on how to use GEDmatch to parse out Native American ancestry !
